note: Saint Vincent and the Grenadines, read on 2026-10-30 in the requirement sheets the Consulate General of Saint Vincent and the Grenadines publishes for non-nationals (svgconsulate.vc, the government's consulate; fees 'as of March 01, 2016 - subject to change'). Fees are in Eastern Caribbean dollars. A Residency Permit is applied for on the form returned to the Office of the Prime Minister (Residency Department) with a police certificate, evidence of means or a letter of support from a person or an employer who sponsors the applicant, and a non-refundable EC$200 application fee, and goes to Cabinet for approval. Temporary residence costs EC$800 a year for CARICOM nationals, EC$1,600 for Commonwealth nationals and EC$2,400 for others (the others' fee written, a year's); permanent residence EC$2,400 for CARICOM and Commonwealth nationals and EC$3,200 for others (others' written), EC$8,000 by reason of an Alien Land-Holding Licence; the EC$200 application fee isn't summed in. A Work Permit is applied for at the Office of the Prime Minister (Work Permit Department) with a letter from the employer and proof the post was advertised, goes to Cabinet, and is issued on a one-time basis for not more than six months, so it isn't renewable and no term is written; anyone asking for more than six months must also apply for a residence permit. Its fee runs by period for non-CARICOM nationals (EC$700 to 30 days up to EC$2,400 over 90 days to a year) and EC$960 a year for CARICOM nationals, so no one fee is written. OECS nationals need neither since 1 August 2011 under the OECS Treaty (their free movement isn't modelled here). Where the temporary residence route's purpose is any (means or a sponsor), it is `general`. No decision time, work rights of the residence permits, or years to permanent residence are stated. The lead took out the temporary residence fee on 2026-10-30: it is charged by the year, and a route's fee is held as what the grant costs, so it is left out.

sources.title: Consulate General of St. Vincent and the Grenadines: Residency Permit (requirements and fees)
sources.said: Complete Residency Permit Application Form (in duplicate) along with the following and Return Application Form to the Office of the Prime Minister (Residency Department): ... the applicant may submit a letter of support from an individual or from his/her employer (if he plans to be employed locally), whereby the employer will accept financial responsibility (sponsor) for the applicant ... The documents will be sent to Cabinet for approval ... As of August 1, 2011 under the OECS Treaty, OECS Nationals are not required to submit work and residence applications ... Fees – (as of March 01, 2016) - subject to change ... CARICOM Nationals EC$800.00 per annum ... Commonwealth Nationals EC$1600.00 per annum ... Others EC$2400.00 per annum ... Others EC$3200.00

sources.title: Consulate General of St. Vincent and the Grenadines: Work Permit (requirements and fees)
sources.said: Return Application Form to the Office of the Prime Minister (Work Permit Department): ... Letter from employer ... Proof that the position applied for has been advertised ... A work permit ONLY is issued on a one-time basis for not more than six (6) months. ... Applicants requesting more than six (6) months for a work permit are required to additionally submit an application for a residence permit. ... For a period up to 30 days EC$700.00 ... For a period over 90 days up to 12 months EC$2400.00
